test_title: SSC Selection Post 2024 (Graduate Level) Official Paper (Held On: 24 Jun, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A, B and C can do the same work in 9 days, 12 days and 18 days, respectively. A started the work and worked for 3 days and left. Then, B joined the work and worked for 3 days and left. Then, C joined the work and completed the work. Find the number of days C took to complete the work.
solution:
**Given:**

A can complete the work in 9 days.

B can complete the work in 12 days.

C can complete the work in 18 days.

A works for 3 days, B works for 3 days, and C completes the rest.

**Formula Used:**

Work done by a person in 1 day = 1 / Number of days to complete work

Total work done = Sum of work done by each person

**Calculation:**

Work done by A in 1 day = 1 / 9

Work done by A in 3 days = 3 × (1 / 9) = 3 / 9 = 1 / 3

Work done by B in 1 day = 1 / 12

Work done by B in 3 days = 3 × (1 / 12) = 3 / 12 = 1 / 4

Total work done by A and B = (1 / 3) + (1 / 4)

(1)/(3) + (1)/(4) = (4 + 3)/(12) = (7)/(12)

Remaining work = 1 - (7 / 12)

1 - (7)/(12) = (12 - 7)/(12) = (5)/(12)

Work done by C in 1 day = 1 / 18

Let the number of days C took to complete the remaining work be x.

Work done by C in x days = x / 18

Remaining work = Work done by C in x days

(5)/(12) = (x)/(18)

⇒ x = (5 / 12) × 18

⇒ x = (5 × 18) / 12

⇒ x = 90 / 12

⇒ x = 7.5

**The number of days C took to complete the work is 7.5 days.**
